title: Bahrain
capsule: In this period Bahrain passed from a nominal dependency of Zand Persia, governed since 1753 by the Bushire-based Al-Madhkur family under Nasr Al-Madhkur, to permanent Arab rule under the Al Khalifa branch of the Bani Utbah confederation. In 1782-83 the Al Khalifa and their allies, based at Zubarah in Qatar, repelled Nasr Al-Madhkur's assault on that town and then invaded and seized the Bahrain archipelago, ending Persian control and installing Ahmed ibn Muhammad Al Khalifa, 'Ahmed al-Fatih,' as the islands' first Al Khalifa ruler. His successors expanded pearl-diving revenues and fortified Riffa against recurring Wahhabi and Omani incursions, cementing a dynasty that has governed Bahrain without interruption since 1783.
